source.note: The orchestrator runs on every request, so trivial is its most frequently exercised cell and was empty. Reuses the `trivial-normalize` fixture -- the trivial tier is cheap precisely because the fixtures already exist -- but asks the orchestrator only to READ and REPORT, never to fix the function `trivial-normalize-v1` scores the Coder on fixing. The fixture's real defect (no trim) is the tempting distraction: the right answer is a one-line reply, and the wrong answer is opening a pipeline, delegating to a specialist, or 'fixing' something nobody asked to fix. `forbids` names the tools that would hand the question to a specialist or a workflow rather than the intention behind them -- the ledger records tool names without arguments, so 'did not investigate further than reading the file' is only checkable as 'did not call these tools', and the prompt says so directly by naming every one of them. The scorer's own `does-not-delegate` reads the same restraint independently, from the console turn tool list (`report.tools`) rather than the ledger -- two channels that must agree, neither of which is the model's own word for what it did.
